profile.name: Shankholi Ray
profile.tagline: I debug errors in code, and occasionally in life’s logic.
profile.headline: Backend Developer · Azure Integration Engineer
profile.intro: I’m a software engineer who likes getting to the bottom of things—whether that means untangling a production issue, making a cloud workflow faster, or building something from an idea. I work with Java, Spring Boot, .NET, Azure, and the MERN stack to help services communicate and data reach the right place.

about: I like figuring things out, whether it’s a DSA problem on LeetCode or a new technology I haven’t used before. I enjoy chess, photography, and editing videos too. I’m trained in Odissi, an Indian classical dance form, and I’m also drawn to spirituality and meditation.
This little world is a tour of what I build, how I work, and what I’m learning. Choose an object to explore a project, visit my workbench, or follow my journey.
skills: Java, Spring Boot, Hibernate/JPA, REST APIs, OAuth, WebSockets, and STOMP · .NET / .NET Core and C#.
Microsoft Azure · Functions, Durable Functions, Service Bus, Event Hubs, Cosmos DB, Blob Storage, API Management (APIM), and Key Vault.
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) · Application deployments through existing Azure DevOps pipelines across Dev, SIT, UAT, pre-production, and production.
Microservices, event-driven and serverless architecture, distributed systems, asynchronous messaging, WebSockets, and STOMP.
Cosmos DB, MongoDB, MySQL · Application Insights, KQL, monitoring and alerts, application logs, Azure Portal, and production troubleshooting.
xUnit, unit testing, code coverage, SonarCloud code-smell analysis, and pull-request reviews.
Java, C#, Python, JavaScript, SQL · Git, GitHub, Postman, Maven, Azure DevOps, YAML, and Swagger / OpenAPI.
MERN: MongoDB, Express, React, and Node.js · JavaScript and Three.js.

highlights: Backend APIs & integrations
Developed REST APIs and event-driven integrations across 20+ .NET Azure Function Apps and five Spring Boot applications on AKS, including Cosmos DB data retrieval and payload mapping.
Messaging performance
Used concurrent dispatch to bring Event Hubs publishing latency to 320–500 ms per message. Reused Service Bus connections to reduce bulk-publishing overhead.
Transaction recovery

Developed a shared retry API and recovery tooling with destination-specific retries, Service Bus dead-letter handling, and duplicate detection. Recovered approximately 500 failed production transactions.
Operational automation
Built .NET console applications and APIs for bulk transfers of approximately 1,000 messages, reducing manual operational work.
Durable workflows
Developed scheduled Azure Durable Functions workflows to filter and aggregate Blob Storage payloads, batching up to 200 JSON files per downstream API request.
Testing & reviews
Wrote xUnit tests, assessed code coverage and code smells with SonarCloud, and performed pull-request reviews.
Release delivery
Handled application deployments across Dev, SIT, UAT, pre-production, and production using existing Azure DevOps pipelines.
Monitoring & diagnosis
Configured Application Insights alerts and KQL queries for interface-specific exception monitoring and transaction-log analysis.

collab.name: Collab Loop
collab.text: A live workspace for shared documents and collaborative whiteboards.
collab.details: A React frontend and Spring Boot backend bring live document editing and shared whiteboards into one workspace. REST APIs and STOMP-over-WebSocket messaging support collaboration; PostgreSQL stores documents and version history, with Flyway migrations.
highlights: Shared whiteboards with pens, colors, and shapes for sketching ideas together
JWT authentication and owner/editor/viewer document sharing
Live document editing, collaborator presence, and version history

readshorts.name: Readshorts
readshorts.text: A publishing and reading space for stories, blogs, and articles.
readshorts.details: A React reading and writing interface backed by Express APIs and MongoDB models. Content can be created, browsed by type and category, and opened in a dedicated reading view.
highlights: Post creation and category-based browsing
Separate flows for stories, blogs, and articles
React frontend connected to Express and MongoDB APIs

restaurants.name: Zomato Clone
restaurants.text: A restaurant discovery and ordering project with a Zomato-inspired interface.
restaurants.details: A React frontend and Express/MongoDB backend support restaurant search, filtering, detail pages, menus, and an ordering interface.
highlights: Filters for location, cuisine, meal type, and price range
Price sorting and paginated search results
Restaurant details, menu selection, and a checkout integration

emotify.name: Emotify
emotify.text: An app that uses facial expressions to recommend music for your mood.
emotify.details: Emotify uses webcam input and emotion-recognition models to track facial expressions and suggest songs based on the detected mood.
highlights: Webcam-based facial-expression recognition
Mood-based song recommendations
Similar-song recommendations from users’ favorite Spotify tracks are coming next

targeted.name: Targeted Ad Project
targeted.text: An ad display that switches campaigns using audience details supplied by an API.
targeted.details: A React frontend requests audience data from a local API and selects matching image or video ads. A Swiper carousel displays the campaign media, with QR links to campaign destinations.
highlights: Image and video campaigns in an autoplay carousel
Campaign selection using audience attributes returned by an API
QR links and fallback content when the API is unavailable

footfall.name: Footfall Dashboard
footfall.text: A dashboard prototype exploring people counts, threshold alerts, and analytics views.
footfall.details: Built with React and Recharts, with tabbed count, alert, and chart views. The current repository uses sample chart data and a fixed people count; live API integration and the heatmap are future work.
highlights: Tabbed navigation between counts, alerts, and analytics
Threshold-based alert display
Responsive area charts using sample data

atlas.name: My Portfolio
atlas.text: Shanks Studio is a portfolio you can visit: a cozy cyberpunk home with stories tucked into everyday objects.
atlas.details: An editable Blender scene brought to the web with Three.js, animated cupboard doors, camera journeys, and a lightweight rigged character.
highlights: Clickable furniture opens projects, skills, and career stories
Animated camera transitions and an orbitable 3D house
Compressed GLB assets, reduced-motion support, and character animation
